lantern_13_001.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_001.text: Day 1564 brought the first full ordinary working morning without the old three-window tower. Hou's received ground dispatch left at its actual hour, and the cold notice stayed beside the public directions. People arrived with habits formed by the old afternoon exchange and had to change their plans. Yue helped a lost visitor find the current receiving desk as an ordinary neighbor. She did not staff an unaccepted fourth alternative or let her own reserve become the missing regional relay. The delay belonged to a town adapting to a real lost capacity.

lantern_13_002.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_002.text: At the river hall, Ren kept the transferred seventy-five old cells in receiving quarantine until the new fixture's qualified tests could occur. Bei Rong's case had passed its cold dimensional inspection, but that did not yet qualify powered service or make every retained cell compatible. Pu installed the accepted ordinary base, and the paid crew checked the actual support before Ma reviewed the seated work position. The tower bracket's cut pieces remained in their own custody elsewhere. The new unit was a new engineered object with its own accepted source, not the old lamp secretly returning through another door.

lantern_13_003.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_003.text: The installation's seventy-two-copper allowance paid sixty for the crew and independent receiving work and twelve for six separate reference cells. Three reference cells supported the specified calibration, and three supported the other named receiving checks. They were separate from the service stock. Three of the seventy-five transferred cells were sampled under that calibrated procedure on Day 1568 and consumed by the actual assessment. Their observed compatibility allowed the remaining seventy-two sealed matching units to be admitted for this new fixture under the received sampling rule. The spent six references and three samples were no longer fuel for future windows.

lantern_13_004.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_004.text: The accepted operating reserve contained two hundred thirty-two copper for service fuel. Seventy-two admitted transferred cells reduced the remaining required service purchase to forty-four cells at two copper each, eighty-eight copper actually paid after receiving. Seventy-two plus forty-four supplied the hundred sixteen planned exchanges in the fifty-eight-day two-window term. The other hundred forty-four copper stayed unspent in the institutions' joint reserve pending an actual later decision. It did not become wages, care money, or another service term simply because the arithmetic left it available. Hou posted actual spend and retained allocation separately.

lantern_13_005.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_005.text: The forty-four new service cells arrived on Day 1571 and passed their destination checks before the stock entered the received tray. Ren completed the fixture's named powered qualification under its own external load and ordinary stop conditions. The qualified service did not use Yue as a battery, nor advance any operator's personal cultivation realm. Its receiving stations had accepted their actual local rosters, while the central sending shifts would be worked by qualified operators Di Rao and Shen Lan. Their supplements came from the separately approved term; regional base wages and relief remained in the paid annual arrangements.

lantern_13_006.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_006.text: Ma's accepted relief work covered particular dates and travel in those rosters. She had not promised to be permanently present at six receiving desks. Lian asked whether her kept evening would survive the new schedule, and she showed her the actual dates before accepting the extra cover. One conflicted with the evening they had chosen. They moved that evening together to a date both could keep, rather than discovering the conflict after supper was cold. The change did not abolish travel fatigue. It made a particular household promise compatible with a particular received job.

lantern_13_007.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_007.text: The clinic's pending collection-subsidy request received its answer during this interval. The clinic's own fund could cover four actual journeys for the woman who had relied on the lost late window, with the ordinary collection service booked on named dates. It could not promise an indefinite free route to every household. The woman accepted the four journeys and asked what would happen afterward. The clerk gave the next review date rather than an invented permanent assurance. Yue heard her thank the clerk and remain worried. A bounded improvement could leave the larger problem visible.

lantern_13_008.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_008.text: Bai Yuan's nursery reopened its lower yard after the flood, with fewer plants and a later expected sale. She had refunded the prepaid orders she could not fulfill, then planted a smaller next tray from actual remaining stock. Bai Min wanted a chair beside the yard because the shop work kept her daughter downstairs. The qualified carer reviewed the ordinary access, and the family moved a chair within the admitted arrangement. Its placement changed the household's mornings; it did not restore the lost plants or remove the care appointments still needed. Yue visited by invitation and bought vegetables elsewhere.

lantern_13_009.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_009.text: The first new receiving operator, Di Rao, had moved to Chime from Ring Meadow with a partner who did not cultivate. His partner, Liu Sen, mended umbrellas and worried that the river hall would swallow every conversation at supper. Di promised to speak about other things and promptly spent their first meal explaining the fixture's admitted reset. Liu listened, then pointed at the leaking window frame in their rented room. Di repaired the ordinary latch the next morning. Living beside a useful post required attention to another person's equally real day.

lantern_13_010.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_010.text: Shen Lan had no enthusiasm for moving. She already rented a room near the river hall and liked the baker who kept her breakfast aside. Her former employer wanted her to accept evening shop accounts after the new shift. She declined because the combined schedule would leave too little ordinary rest. The former employer hired someone else and complained publicly that qualification made workers proud. Shen corrected him only once. She had accepted a bounded day and needed the rest that made it workable. The town could live with his disappointment without making her prove humility through exhaustion.

lantern_13_011.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_011.text: On Day 1569, before the opening, the two operators walked the receiving route with Hou and found a household instruction addressed to an old stair desk. The sender had copied an earlier cover without checking its current receiving office. Hou contacted the admitted receiving party through the ordinary ground clerk and corrected the address before the new service began. The cover's actual recipient remained private. Yue watched the conversation from outside while waiting for another errand. A new fixture could inherit old clerical habits, so competent people still needed to read what lay in their hands.

lantern_13_012.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_012.text: Ren's final qualification required an actual ordinary stop under a changed input condition at the new fixture. Shen did not anticipate the interruption correctly on her first dry explanation. Ren sent her back to the route sheet and tested the explanation again after the correction, before any powered attempt. The later named powered check stopped and released ordinarily. That evidence belonged to Shen's particular fixture qualification. Yue's earlier successful short route did not clear Shen, and Shen's later receiving result did not advance Yue. Their work was connected by an institution, not by interchangeable personal achievements.

lantern_13_013.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_013.text: Outside the river hall a child asked Di where the light lived while the fixture was cold. Di described the sealed external cells and showed the ordinary public diagram, leaving the locked stock cupboard closed. The child asked whether a cell was alive. Di said it was a finite prepared source for the instrument's activity, not a creature trapped waiting for rescue. He did not invite the child to touch a contact to make the explanation vivid. The conversation ended with the child drawing a square cupboard, disappointed by its decidedly unromantic shape.

lantern_13_014.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_014.text: Zheng Lin's cough worsened on Day 1566. Bao booked the ordinary practitioner he had already been seeing, who assessed the changed condition and arranged further qualified care. The family paid the disclosed charges from its own accepted care funds and requested help with specific meals and errands, not with an imaginary charged cure. Yue collected a paid soup order after her ordinary walk. Zheng thanked her and complained about its lack of pepper. Bao asked the practitioner before changing his food. His preferences mattered without overruling the actual advice about his present body.

lantern_13_015.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_015.text: He still wanted to see the new receiver's base. Ren offered an admitted measured drawing rather than inviting him to a tiring installation site. Zheng said a photograph never showed how a bracket felt under the hand. Pu drew the dimensions and wrote the observed inspection result beside them. That was not the sensation Zheng wanted, and it was useful information he could actually receive in his room. He examined the page for an hour, then put it down because reading had tired him. His interest survived longer that day than his energy for satisfying it.

lantern_13_016.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_016.text: Bao sent Wei a family letter on Day 1567 by a paid ground dispatch, describing the worsening illness and the actual invitation to visit if his employer could release him. The letter reached Wei on Day 1572. He obtained an accepted unpaid family absence from Day 1573 through Day 1593, booked the ordinary eight-day outward coach, and paid its fare from received savings. The return booking left him five local days between two real eight-day journeys. His uncle's condition would not suspend the coach's road time or the employer's actual leave dates.

lantern_13_017.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_017.text: Yue knew the departure had been booked and wanted it to mean Wei would arrive in time for a conversation. It meant he would arrive on Day 1580 if the ordinary journey held. Bao had not promised her uncle another fourteen days of life by sending a letter. The practitioner's qualified care continued, addressing actual symptoms and comfort, with the family present as Zheng wished. There was uncertainty the dates could not solve. Yue disliked the helplessness and kept doing the concrete errand Bao asked for, instead of converting that dislike into a claim to know a hidden remedy.

lantern_13_018.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_018.text: On Day 1570 Zheng asked Bao to bring the cracked lens from its shelf. He held it briefly, then returned it to her because his hand was tired. He wanted her to keep it if she wanted it, and sell other personally owned tools under the ordinary household arrangement after checking their condition. The association's retained bracket plate did not belong to that estate. Bao wrote his stated wishes and asked him which details he still wanted changed. He chose who could receive his own objects without making every artifact in town an inheritance for a favored visitor.

lantern_13_019.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_019.text: He asked Yue whether the great circuit had become easier after the failed wrist day. She said the stop response was more reliable in the actual short preparation, and the full circuit remained unqualified. He nodded, pleased by the distinction. His room did not become a place where Yue could claim a comforting stage-nine success that had not happened. She told him about Pu Mei's paper tower instead. He laughed once at the wide cardboard base and coughed afterward. Bao ended the visit when he needed rest, and Yue left on the agreed ordinary terms.

lantern_13_020.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_020.text: Shao met Yue in the public room on Day 1572 for a scheduled dry planning conversation. She was a woman in her fifties, with a narrow lined face and salt-and-pepper hair tied in a practical bun. Her muted teal working robe had brown cuffs marked by chalk, not ceremonial embroidery. She looked at Yue's actual sleep and errands before discussing new course dates. A difficult family interval could affect a learner's condition without turning its grief into a qualifying trial. They postponed the prospective live block rather than asking Yue to demonstrate resilience through a powered appointment.

lantern_13_021.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_021.text: The postponed booking had not been paid or staffed yet, so no accepted cell was spent by that decision. Yue continued ordinary dry explanation only when rested, and kept her stage-eight qualification within its existing scope. Shao did not tell her that emotional steadiness would heal Zheng or that mastery of a circuit would allow a person to escape age. She asked which ordinary commitments Yue could actually meet this week. Yue named meals, errands, and a library return. Those were manageable, real actions in days when a greater ambition had no useful immediate task.

lantern_13_022.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_022.text: On Day 1573 the practitioner's latest assessment found Zheng's condition worsening despite the received ordinary care. Bao listened to the current options and chose the arrangements Zheng wanted for comfort and company. The family had an actual paid carer for the times they could not themselves remain. Yue brought a small purchased bowl of soup and stayed in the public room while Bao decided whether a visit would help. Zheng slept through that afternoon. The unopened soup went to the household kitchen under its ordinary food arrangement, not beside the bed as a symbol someone would later claim he received.

lantern_13_023.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_023.text: On the evening before his outward family letter would reach Wei, Zheng had asked Yue for ordinary news from the market. She described Sun Luo's changed shop arrow and the cart driver's repaired pin. He complained that nobody made things thick enough anymore. Yue reminded him of the tray edge he wanted thinner. He smiled and said exceptions were the mark of an experienced opinion. The conversation did not contain a final secret doctrine. It contained his recognizable teasing, received on an evening when he could still choose to make it.

lantern_13_024.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_024.text: Bao told Yue later that she treasured that ordinary account more than some of the formal thanks offered at the funeral. She had heard him tease people for decades and would miss the annoying part too. She did not need him remembered as a patient saint to justify loving him. Yue had once wanted every recovered check and successful stop to make her more admirable. Listening to Bao, she began to see how affection could survive facts a flattering account would omit. It could also end in grief without being retroactively judged a poor investment.

lantern_13_025.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_025.text: When the practitioner explained the worsening condition, Bao asked which ordinary comfort measures had evidence for this situation and which were merely customary. Some customs mattered to Zheng as chosen practices even without curing the illness. She kept those he wanted, rejected a costly untested remedy promoted by a visiting seller, and continued the qualified care. The seller promised confidence rather than a reproducible observation. Bao had finite money for actual needs. Refusing his pitch did not mean she accepted the death eagerly. It meant his promise had not earned the money she could use more concretely.

lantern_13_026.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_026.text: Zheng Lin died on Day 1574 with Bao and the qualified practitioner present. The practitioner received the actual time and condition in the ordinary death record. The care had addressed symptoms and comfort; it had not prevented this death. Yue arrived later for the errand she had promised and learned what had happened from Bao. No reserve reading, relay window, hidden lens, or later cultivation certificate returned him to the room. His cough was no longer an inconvenience to schedule around. A living person with unfinished preferences and ordinary attachments was permanently gone.

lantern_13_027.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_027.text: The seller returned after the death and said the family should have purchased sooner. Fan ordered him out of the private gathering before Bao had to answer. Yue was grateful for that direct ordinary intervention. The seller had no evidence that his remedy would have altered the outcome and no authority to assign the family blame. The gathering continued without inviting him to debate grieving people for an audience. Bao later thanked Fan for protecting the room and still declined his larger public memorial proposal. Gratitude for one act did not require accepting every offer from its author.

lantern_13_028.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_028.text: Bao asked Yue to take a short family notice to the paid dispatch for Wei's receiving address. Wei was already on the road, so the receiving clerk could hold the notice for his actual arrival under the family's admitted instruction. The notice did not reach backward in time to shorten the booked coach journey. Yue paid the posted dispatch fee from the small errand sum Bao provided, returned the change, and did not read the private enclosure beyond the address she was told to copy. The useful act did not make the helplessness disappear.

lantern_13_029.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_029.text: The new receiver opened its authorized service on Day 1575 after actual qualification and accepted rosters. Two daily windows began under finite external fuel and paid staff, with fewer opportunities than the old service's three. Hou's public notice named that difference plainly. Bao did not attend the opening, and the institution did not delay its accepted regional work because one family was mourning. Yue saw both events share a day without becoming each other's explanation. A received new fixture could serve living households while remaining utterly unable to return Zheng's voice to his niece.

lantern_13_030.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_030.text: The family arranged the ordinary funeral under its own accepted funds and local customs. Bao invited the people she wanted present and declined a public tower memorial inside the private gathering. Fan had meant the proposed speeches kindly. She wanted an account of her uncle that included his bad temper, gifts, missed meals, and absurd insistence that every tray edge could be improved. The tower belonged in that life without becoming its whole subject. Fan accepted the refusal and came as an ordinary acquaintance, bringing the food the household had actually asked for.

lantern_13_031.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_031.text: Yue helped set chairs within the room's permitted capacity. She was not given a new social or cultivation rank for grieving competently. Bao asked her to leave one chair free beside the window, then changed her mind because the emptiness hurt. They moved it into the circle. Nobody treated the changed arrangement as a failure to know the proper ritual. A funeral could contain practical revisions made by the person living its loss. Yue held the spare cloth while Bao chose where to put the lens, still wrapped and still cracked.

lantern_13_032.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_032.text: Zheng's remembered repair stories differed between speakers. Lu Jien said the older man had taught him to stop pretending a contact could be fixed by pressing harder. Pu recalled a time Zheng himself pressed harder and ruined a small part. The room laughed with Bao's permission, then fell quiet. These accounts did not need to be reconciled into a man incapable of making the mistake he later warned against. His knowledge had a history, and his history included errors. Yue missed the possibility of asking him which version he would contest.

lantern_13_033.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_033.text: The funeral ended with its actual attendees leaving and the family staying. Wei had not arrived yet. Bao chose not to postpone every private act until an ordinary road could deliver him. She kept a separate gathering for his accepted visit and a place where he could sit with the object his uncle had left. Her choice was not a claim that he should feel no regret for the journey's timing. It was a way to let the living household continue its necessary arrangements without asking the dead man's condition to wait for a timetable.

lantern_13_034.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_034.text: He Pu asked whether she wanted to read something at the funeral. She did not, and Bao had asked for a smaller private gathering. He respected the refusal. On the next school afternoon he rearranged a lesson because several pupils knew Zheng as the man who complained about their paper models. He acknowledged the death plainly and offered the ordinary choice to talk or continue the reading task. Pu Mei wanted to continue first and talk afterward. A teacher did not have to turn every child's quietness into evidence that a single prescribed ritual had worked.

lantern_13_035.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_035.text: Pu Mei's question afterward was whether the paper tower should be taken apart too. Its cold colored window had never supplied the relay's service, and its cardboard base was not the retired metal bracket. Pu said she could keep it, alter it, or use its materials for another actual model. She kept it for the week and moved the volcano beside it. The decision did not preserve Zheng or the old tower's three windows. It preserved something she had made with people still available to argue about where it should sit.

lantern_13_036.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_036.text: Yan Di wanted to perform the elephant story for Bao to cheer her. Lian asked Bao first. She said she could not enjoy a performance that evening and would like him to bring it another day if he still wanted. Yan was hurt, then asked whether she disliked the puppet. Lian explained the actual refusal without making Bao comfort the child for declining entertainment during grief. Yan kept the puppet at home. A possible later invitation remained possible, and a presently unwanted kindness remained unwanted even when its author had meant well.

lantern_13_037.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_037.text: On Day 1578 the first new service report showed six completed exchanges across three two-window days. The finite stock had been charged for those six, leaving one hundred ten accepted service cells. Di Rao recorded an interruption that ended one private message before its admitted length; the receiving clerk arranged the sender's longer letter by ground dispatch. A completed staffed exchange did not mean every desired sentence had traveled. Yue read the public total and let its modest reality stand. There was no light in those numbers that belonged to Zheng's empty chair.

lantern_13_038.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_038.text: The opening gathering had no grand banquet after the earlier farewell's strained food estimate. Each institution sent its received representative, the paid operators performed their tasks, and residents watched from the permitted public area. Chao Yun came as a neighbor and did not sing without a booked fee or her own explicit offer. She enjoyed listening for once. Yu sold the ordinary food she had actually prepared for expected customers, not a compulsory celebration ration. Some people left early because the opening took longer than their lunch break. The service still began with its actual staff.

lantern_13_039.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_039.text: A woman named Lu Fen brought a private instruction she hoped would reach her sister before the next market. The first new window could send its admitted short form, but the sister's local receiving clerk would distribute it on the next ordinary round. The instruction therefore missed the earliest market despite a completed relay exchange. Lu had understood the light's travel time and not the staffed delivery time. Hou updated the public explanation after asking her permission to use the anonymous confusion. The new unit's two windows did not magically erase its receiving institutions' ordinary schedules.

lantern_13_040.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_040.text: Fan said the explanation made the service sound slow again. Deng asked whether he would prefer a faster phrase that cost another resident an actual market opportunity. Fan frowned and admitted he had relied on the receiving round himself more than once. He added its departure time to his own cart notice. The correction was useful beyond the institution that first made it. Yue saw a merchant accept a small accurate constraint without surrendering every wish for a bigger service. His demands would continue, and his next customer would at least find a clearer sign.

lantern_13_041.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_041.text: Yue applied for ordinary work at the school when the family errands allowed it. He Pu had a later editing-and-route-review task beginning Day 1590, thirty-nine calendar days through Day 1628 at three copper each. It would use admitted public teaching sheets and checked routes, with two-hour duty mornings and paid weekly rest. The school required neither a private workshop appendix nor Bai Min's household file. Yue's earlier copying and survey work supplied actual references available on every history of her recent choice. He accepted her for a hundred seventeen-copper term, conditional on the named ordinary schedule.

lantern_13_042.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_042.text: The job would not begin before Day 1590, and the school paid on received work rather than as an immediate consolation for grief. Yue planned the intervening days from money already earned under her chosen completed term. Its wage had differed from the other offers, so the size of her training cushion differed too. She left the prospective live course unbooked until living costs and the next received payment were clear. A later common employer could recognize qualifications shared by her earlier copying and survey without granting her all the relationships she had declined in the transition decision.

lantern_13_043.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_043.text: Ma visited Bao after a received relief day with her sister Lian. She brought the requested plain meal, not the funeral speech she had abandoned in an unfinished draft. They ate together quietly until Bao told the story of Zheng misjudging the cane sleeve's fit and blaming its maker. Ma laughed because she had heard the complaint herself. Their visit lasted an hour, then ended because Bao wanted sleep. The ordinary limit made another later visit possible. It did not diminish the affection because no one remained until exhaustion made departure feel like betrayal.

lantern_13_044.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_044.text: Han Tao offered a vegetable delivery for the household's next week at its ordinary price, and Bao accepted two specified baskets. Han did not assume grief meant the household wanted daily unsolicited food. She asked which vegetables could actually be used and brought those. Yue collected the first basket while Bao handled the tool buyer. The task gave her hands something useful and familiar to do. It was not a cure for the empty room. A life after a death could consist partly of small received arrangements that left the loss unnamed for an afternoon.

lantern_13_045.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_045.text: At the new receiver, Shen's first scheduled relief day tested whether the accepted rota existed outside its paper. The named qualified alternate arrived after paid travel, performed the received shift, and left Shen able to rest. The institution recorded the actual cover and cost. It did not ask Shen to stay nearby unpaid in case the alternate felt nervous. She ate with Liu and Di that evening and complained about the alternate's excessively neat handwriting. Her complaint was sociable, and her rest was real. An alternative mattered when someone actually did the work it promised.

lantern_13_046.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_046.text: Di and Liu argued over the window latch again because Di had repaired the wrong loose part. The rain still entered. Liu hired the landlady's ordinary carpenter under the room's accepted maintenance arrangement, and Di stayed to describe what he had done. The carpenter corrected the latch and a separate worn frame seal. Di's good intention had not been enough, and the room did not need him humiliated to receive a competent repair. Yue heard Liu tell the story at tea, where everyone enjoyed the contrast between a qualified operator and an ordinary stubborn window.

lantern_13_047.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_047.text: Yu finally received the restaurant owner's answer about the proposed cooking fixture. The summer accounts supported a smaller ordinary kitchen repair first, while the powered purchase remained deferred. Her bounded qualification stayed earned for its named task, though the device was not installed in this kitchen. She asked for a wage review based on her actual cooking work rather than the unreceived fixture proposal. The owner agreed to review that separately on a stated date. Yue admired the distinction: an unused qualification did not make all her present labor valueless, and a future machine did not already exist.

lantern_13_048.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_048.text: The nursery's new tray sprouted unevenly. Bai Yuan sold the accepted healthy plants and kept the weaker ones out of fulfilled orders. Bai Min insisted the crooked plant at the edge was the prettiest. Her daughter let her keep it for the household, where its irregularity was a chosen preference rather than a falsely advertised product. Yue saw it near the shaded chair on her next invited visit. Its leaves leaned toward the light from the lane. No one called it the return of the lost first tray. It was another plant, alive on another day.

lantern_13_049.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_049.text: Rui's separate orchard cloth order reached its actual buyer during the mourning interval. She had worried that speaking about a successful sale would be tasteless near Bao's loss. Bao asked her to tell the ordinary news anyway; the household did not want every visitor to arrive wearing only funeral silence. Rui described the buyer choosing the blue border over the green. Bao liked green better and said the buyer had poor taste. The opinion sounded so like her uncle's contrarian judgments that she laughed, then cried. Both responses belonged to the living conversation.

lantern_13_050.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_050.text: Yue went home afterward and opened her own route notebook without beginning a practice. The old failed delay, later recovered stops, and future threshold remained there, dated and unchanged by the funeral. Beside the notebook lay the new school contract whose ordinary work began on Day 1590. She would have something useful to do, and later actual course planning to resume. Those prospects did not require her to pretend she had learned a profound law from Zheng's death. She had lost an acquaintance she liked. Bao and Wei had lost much more, in ways she could not measure for them.

lantern_13_051.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_051.text: Her mother's next letter said the apprentice cousin had arrived and occupied the spare bed on the accepted dates. Yue was glad he had a place and disappointed that imagining her own return now required another conversation. She wrote a short answer after supper, asking about the ordinary household repairs and promising no journey she had not booked.

lantern_13_052.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_052.text: Wei arrived on Day 1580 carrying the smaller repaired tray. He learned the held family notice at the inn's receiving desk before anyone tried to let his arrival become a joyful surprise. Bao met him in the public room and stayed while he read. The tray had lost part of its original rim and now rested evenly. Its repair had been completed on an ordinary workshop afternoon before his coach departed. It did not become an offering received by Zheng after death. Bao chose to keep it in the household, where living cups could still stand on it.

lantern_13_053.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_053.text: Wei was angry that he had obeyed the earlier apprenticeship break and left before the final service day. Bao said he had not caused the illness by returning to accepted work. He knew that and remained angry. Yue listened rather than offering a calculation that would abolish his regret. The first visit had contained real conversation; the second had missed its possibility. Those were both facts. He could remember his uncle's explanation of the bracket and still wish he had heard another one, without a story making the missed conversation secretly occur.

lantern_13_054.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_054.text: For the remaining local days of his accepted absence, Wei helped Bao sort the personally owned tools. They checked actual condition and kept the pieces the household wanted, offering others for sale under the stated wishes. The sale did not transfer the association's bracket plate or resurrect the old lens mount. Yue declined an offered small fitting because she had no use for it and did not want another person's grief to choose her possessions. Bao appreciated the direct answer. A useful refusal could leave an object available to someone who actually needed it.

lantern_13_055.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_055.text: At the tool sorting, Pu checked a worn file and found it unsuitable for its original precise work. Wei wanted to keep every tool his uncle had handled. Bao asked where he would put them and whether he wanted them for use or memory. He chose two safe small tools and the repaired tray, leaving the rest to the accepted sorting plan. The worn file was marked as a retained ordinary keepsake rather than sold as a working tool. Memory could justify keeping it without making its condition suitable for a buyer who depended on precision.

lantern_13_056.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_056.text: Bao sold a usable pair of clamps to a local maker at an agreed price after inspection. The sale paid a portion of the funeral's actual costs, and she kept the household's accepted care bills separate. Yue helped carry the light wrapped clamps to the buyer within her ordinary limit. The buyer did not claim the tools carried their previous owner's skill. He used them for a received job later that week and still had to measure his work. An inherited or purchased object could make a task possible without transmitting a person into whoever held it.

lantern_13_057.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_057.text: Wei went to see the retained bracket plate before his return journey. Hou showed him its public label and the actual exhibit room where it would remain cold. The young man asked to touch it and was permitted after the keeper explained the allowed handling. He traced the stamp, then asked about one repair his uncle had described differently. Hou directed him to the admitted dated history instead of inventing a reconciliation. Wei copied the citation for himself. He could pursue a question after the person who raised it died, but could no longer ask that person what he meant.

lantern_13_058.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_058.text: The apprenticeship employer sent an ordinary acknowledgment of Wei's return booking to the receiving inn. It confirmed the unpaid absence and the date his place would remain available. Wei read it with relief and resentment. The practical security mattered, and the clock on grief felt cruel. Bao said the employer had kept the agreed term; Wei could decide later whether he still wanted the apprenticeship, but should not imagine silence purchased an indefinite place. He kept the booking. His return would carry regret as well as the small tools, without a promise that work would immediately feel normal.

lantern_13_059.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_059.text: The cracked lens stayed on Bao's shelf in a new safe place. She did not restore its missing street view or demand that every visitor admire it. Sometimes she wanted to look at it, and sometimes she covered it. Yue recognized those ordinary changes without turning them into stages of a recovery that would conclude in an intact object. Bao's grief could alter how she used the room. It would not reverse the death. The household continued with a chair moved, a tray repaired, and fewer voices answering at supper.

lantern_13_060.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_060.text: On Day 1583 Shao reviewed Yue's ordinary condition before agreeing to revisit course planning the following month. Yue's sleep had improved but remained interrupted, and she had done no live practice during the family interval. They kept preparation dry and did not use the funeral as a changed-condition exam. A relevant future trial would require a qualified actual route, current sampling, recovered ordinary conditions, and the next day's tissue check. A difficult personal event was not automatically evidence for those things. Yue appreciated the clarity more now than she had when a course seemed capable of solving every uncertainty.

lantern_13_061.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_061.text: One small household gathering before Wei's return included the repaired tray on the table. It held four ordinary cups while Bao and her nephew argued about whether he should take the larger tool bag. Yue kept to the permitted light errand bag and declined to carry it for him as a gesture. The coach's booked luggage provision could carry it if he actually chose to take it. Wei kept the smaller selection, and the unused space held food that would survive the first road day. Practical choices continued, even in the presence of an absence nobody could fix.

lantern_13_062.speaker: narrator
lantern_13_062.text: Day 1584 ended with Wei's return coach still booked for Day 1586, after his five local days. Bao invited Yue to an ordinary meal on his last evening rather than asking her to stay through every remaining hour. The river-hall unit continued its two paid windows, the tower stayed permanently cold, and the public ground route kept its slower departures. Zheng remained dead. The town's functioning alternatives made some tasks possible for the living. They left the family's actual loss untouched, and Yue could begin another day without pretending those two truths canceled one another.
